A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same watermark-based attribution framework and A-BSTA algorithm. Text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original image detection and attribution experiments, robustness tests, watermark-selection comparisons, and AWT text-watermarking experiments.

after.justification: V4 retains original image and text experiments and adds watermark implementations, forgery tests, comparison controls, and supplementary empirical analyses.

M1.justification: The watermark assignment, detection rule, nearest-match attribution, and A-BSTA procedures remain unchanged. V4 Section 8 adds an optional inference extension that aggregates attribution decisions by majority vote when multiple pieces of content are known to originate from one user.

E1.justification: The original image corpora and WikiText-2 coverage are retained. V4 adds limited scenarios involving forgery of non-watermarked COCO images and attribution using multiple pieces of content from one user. Evaluating additional watermark implementations does not itself add datasets or domains.

E2.justification: V4 adds Hash alongside Random and A-BSTA in Table 7, and empirically compares user-aware detection against single-watermark detection in Figure 5. The original Random/NRG/A-BSTA comparisons remain. StegaStamp and PRC serve as underlying watermark implementations rather than competing attribution algorithms.

E3.justification: V4 substantially expands evaluation configurations through StegaStamp and PRC, restricting PRC to open Stable Diffusion. Added protocols include forgery testing on 1,000 COCO images with forgery success, PSNR, and FID metrics, four single-watermark controls, and multi-content aggregation. The original dataset splits, image resolution, and principal attribution metrics remain.

E4.justification: V4 adds analyses of forgery resistance, user-aware versus single-watermark detection, accuracy across individual watermarks, decoded-bit bias, and multi-content aggregation. Conversely, v2 Figure 10's standard-training HiDDeN robustness control is removed. Existing parameter sweeps, adversarial robustness tests, and theoretical-versus-empirical comparisons are largely retained through relocation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, statistical error bars, or significance tests. The added per-watermark plots describe experimental variation without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V4 adds StegaStamp/PRC results in Figure 2 and zero forgery success for Stable Signature, WAM, and PRC in Table 6. Table 7 reports similarities of 0.875 for Random and Hash versus 0.734 for A-BSTA at 100,000 watermarks. Section 8 reports TAR of 0.998 before aggregation and 1.000 with aggregation. These are added comparisons; original numerical tables and retained plotted curves remain unchanged, while standard-training robustness results are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, watermarking assumptions, four theorems, two corollaries, proofs, optimization formulation, and complexity analysis retain their substance. Their relocation and revised equation formatting do not introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first systematic study of watermark-based user attribution, probabilistic performance bounds, and theoretically motivated watermark selection. The central accuracy and conditional robustness claims remain. Additional watermark evaluations provide supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: V4 substantially expands discussion of privacy, trusted verification, forgery, hash selection, steganography, C2PA, and limitations under many-query attacks. It also removes v2 Section 7.4's explanation linking differing black-box robustness findings to watermark length, decoder capacity, and stronger training. Existing service-level and hierarchical attribution discussions are retained in Appendix O.

D1.justification: V4 omits v2's explicit ResNet18 decoder choice, default HiDDeN training disclosure, and image post-processing threshold exception of 0.85. These omissions do not establish actual implementation changes. AWT hyperparameters and adversarial-training details remain. V4 adds a reproducibility statement promising code and dataset release, without documenting an actual release.

R1.justification: V4 substantially updates the image-watermarking survey with work including PRC, Gaussian Shading, WAM, LAWA, and FreqMark. New discussions position the framework relative to forgery attacks, steganography, and C2PA. The original relationship to farthest-string algorithms remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 places theoretical performance analysis before watermark selection, rewrites the introduction and related work, consolidates experimental sections, and moves substantial definitions, explanations, analyses, and text experiments into appendices. It also adds discussion and reproducibility sections and changes the title, author list, and publication header.

P2.justification: V4 expands the ranked-attribution display into three watermark panels, splits and regroups retained comparison plots, and relocates many figures and tables. It adds diagnostic plots and forgery/hash tables, removes the standard-training robustness figure, and replaces common-post-processing examples, including JPEG Q=60 with Q=20. ICLR formatting and wrapped figures substantially alter the layout.

improvement.justification: V4 provides better evidence that the framework applies beyond HiDDeN through StegaStamp and PRC evaluations, while the single-watermark and Hash controls strengthen its empirical justification. The expanded privacy and security discussion also improves assessment of applicability. These gains are partly offset by removing the standard-training robustness control and important decoder and threshold disclosures. The unchanged core theory and results, together with these reproducibility losses, support a limited overall improvement.
